findings.shape: Selected laterally attached shell-like bodies expose paired radial split pseudolamellar folds beneath thin hairy caps. The woody orientation is a selected contextual study, not the photographed individual.
findings.surface: Pale densely modeled hairs, lighter margins and pinkish-grey paired lower folds replace blank dark undersides. Original relief and pigment are retained across actions.
findings.movement: Stationary same fruit bodies with an enlarged authored spore overlay. Moisture-induced enrollment and gill splitting are biological context only; no working hygroscopic mechanics are claimed.
findings.evidenceScope: Actual Bernard Spragg NZ photograph and selected Adelaide description compared. Selected review text/caption discusses moisture response; its reprinted figure was not redistributed or used as a photographic asset. Macro appearance alone does not resolve cryptic lineages.
corrections: Added paired split lower folds and denser short pale hairs.
Batched stationary fold geometry for responsiveness and exposed lower folds through the underside camera.
findings.residual: The seven cap arrangement is more regular and less crowded than the photograph. Fine split-fold edges, branching/anastomosis, hyphal hairs and tissue optics are incomplete. No measured moisture response or independent lineage identification.
